(i) For d<=6 (q=7) and d<=4 (q=13), every computed c_k with k>(d+1)/2 lies in span{c_i, i<=(d+1)/2} with m-independent coefficients (F2 exact to d=6, F1 exact to d=5), so the base probe at k>d re-expresses blocks with dual length <= N-(d+1)/2; the cap h<=1-M/2 follows given the cited law h=r/N; the pre-registered outcome-B threshold is not met at N=2. (ii) At dual length 0 the probe equals wt*q^d times the Moebius-weighted sum of the row weight exactly for any weight (independently confirmed on a new target), and the row is kappa times the conjugate (mu*w)-twisted sextic row exactly. (iii) By Cauchy-Schwarz a diagonal-level row bound bounds the Moebius sum by the trivial bound divided by wt (wt<=q-1 at computed sizes); the mu-weighted row exceeds the diagonal by a bounded factor (up to 6.3 unmarked, about 3 in the h>1 region) while target rows approach the diagonal for N=2..4. lesson: The h>1 vertices of the ledger at lx<l are real in the function-field model, but their low input (diagonal-level mean square of unreflected marked rows for N'<=d<2N') contains the coherent term, which is the squared signal. It is false for the Moebius-twisted weight with coefficients of the same modulus, so no sieve-type estimate can supply it. The ledger's sub-1/2 vertices came from omitting that term. Raw thresholds on h at N<=4 are dominated by O(1/N) terms, because the sixth-power count is constant for r<=5. Process: for about ten minutes my server requests summed to 18 cores against the 16-core cap, and two local runs bypassed memcap (one killed at 1.1 GB); both are recorded in RESULT.md section 9.
